categories.name: Client CRMs
categories.title: Photography CRM & Client Management Software
categories.desc: Inquiries, contracts, invoices, questionnaires, and client email in one place.
intro: A photography CRM handles the business side of your studio: inquiries, bookings, contracts, invoices, questionnaires, and client communication, so you spend less time on admin and more behind the camera. The best one for you depends on what you need most. Some are built for deep automation, some for simple booking, some specifically for European VAT and GDPR compliance.

When choosing, look at: automated workflows (emails, contracts, payment reminders), a branded client portal, contracts with e-signatures, invoicing and online payments, scheduling, and, if you shoot in the UK or EU, correct VAT handling and a signable data-processing agreement. Pricing matters too, some tools charge a flat monthly fee while others scale with use.

categories.name: Gallery Delivery
categories.title: Client Gallery Software for Photographers
categories.desc: Delivering finished galleries, downloads, proofing, and in-gallery print sales.
intro: Client gallery software is where your finished photos go to be delivered, viewed, downloaded, and often bought. A good platform makes your galleries feel like an extension of your brand: it loads fast, downloads cleanly, and sells prints without you chasing anyone.

When choosing, look at: a branded, password-protected gallery, favoriting and proofing tools, full-resolution and watermarked download options, a built-in print store (and whether it takes a commission on sales), storage that fits your shooting volume, and a clean mobile experience, since most clients open their gallery on a phone. Pricing almost always scales with storage, so compare platforms at your real volume, not the headline entry price.

categories.name: AI Culling & Editing
categories.title: AI Culling & Editing Software for Photographers
categories.desc: Selecting keepers, applying your edit, and retouching across large shoots.
intro: AI culling and editing software automates the slowest parts of post-production: selecting the keepers from thousands of shots, applying your editing style across a whole gallery, and retouching portraits. Used well, these tools cut hours off every wedding or portrait session.

It helps to be clear about three different jobs. Culling is picking the best frames and removing blinks, blurs and duplicates. Editing is applying your color and tone across the set. Retouching is the close-up work on skin, glare and backgrounds. Some tools are excellent at one of these; some do all three. When comparing, weigh culling accuracy, editing quality (skin tones especially), whether the tool runs offline or in the cloud, and the pricing model, a flat monthly fee versus per-photo pricing changes the cost a lot depending on your volume.

verdict.headline: Aftershoot is the strongest all-in-one AI workflow tool for high-volume photographers, and the best value if you shoot a lot. It culls, edits, and retouches in one offline app at a flat, unlimited price, so a huge wedding costs the same to process as a small portrait session.
verdict.bestFor: Wedding, event, and portrait photographers drowning in RAW files who want predictable costs and offline processing.
verdict.elsewhere: If editing quality matters more than culling, Imagen edits better; if you want to keep full manual control of selections, Narrative suits you more.
verdict.bottom: For culling at volume, it's a top pick. The editing is good and improving, but the culling is the reason to buy.

It learns your style from your past catalogs and applies it across a whole gallery, with skin tones that reviewers single out as its standout strength.

chooseIf.text: you live in Lightroom Classic, shoot moderate volume, and want the strongest style matching. Pay-as-you-go pricing is economical for seasonal or lower volume, while high-volume solo shooters can opt for Limitless ($129/mo annual) or switch to Aftershoot’s flat $360/yr editing.

articles.pricingAssumption: Aftershoot Edit is a flat $360/year ($30/mo annual). Imagen offers Pay-As-You-Go ($0.05/photo base editing, or $0.07–$0.09 with modular AI tools) and a flat Limitless subscription ($1,548/year, or $129/mo annual) for eligible solo photographers. On base editing ($0.05/photo), Aftershoot Edit breaks even with Imagen PAYG at 7,200 edited photos a year (600/month); with AI crop and straighten ($0.07/photo), the break-even is 5,143 photos a year (~428/month). Solo photographers delivering higher volume can choose Imagen Limitless or Aftershoot's flat tiers (Checked October 2026).
